future_tenses_plan.structure: Be going to (Future prediction based on evidence)
future_tenses_plan.example: Look at those dark clouds; it is going to rain.
I am going to study a Master's degree next year.

future_tenses_plan.structure: Present Continuous (Future plan with someone else / appointment)
future_tenses_plan.example: I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow at 5 PM.
The Prime Minister is to visit Spain next month.

future_tenses_plan.structure: Present Simple (Event fixed in a timetable - films, transports, concerts, exams)
future_tenses_plan.example: The train to London leaves at 8:00 AM.

future_tenses_plan.structure: to be + due to + inf (Expected event)
future_tenses_plan.example: The exam is due to start in ten minutes.

future_tenses_noplan.structure: Future Simple (Make a future offer - Shall we/I)
future_tenses_noplan.example: Shall I open the window for you?

future_tenses_noplan.structure: Future Simple (Universal facts / future factual statements)
future_tenses_noplan.example: The sun will rise at 6:30 AM tomorrow.

future_tenses_noplan.structure: Future Simple (Make a future prediction without evidence)
future_tenses_noplan.example: I think robots will do all the housework in 2050.
I hope she will pass the driving test.

future_tenses_noplan.structure: Future Simple (Spontaneous decision made at the moment of speaking)
future_tenses_noplan.example: We are out of milk? I will go to the supermarket right now.

modal_verbs_future.example: It might rain later, so take an umbrella.

modal_verbs_future.structure: Probability 1 (may / might / could + well + base form)
modal_verbs_future.example: She may well get the promotion; she has worked very hard.
They are likely to win the match tomorrow.

modal_verbs_future.structure: Probability 3 (There is a little / slight / strong / some likelihood + of + -ing)
modal_verbs_future.example: There is a strong likelihood of him passing the exam.

modal_verbs_future.structure: Probability 4 (There is a likelihood + that clause)
modal_verbs_future.example: There is a strong likelihood that he will pass the exam.
He is bound to complain about the food; he never likes anything.

cambridge_speaking_strategies.structure: There is a strong likelihood that [subject] will increasingly [verb base] in the coming years.
cambridge_speaking_strategies.example: There is a strong likelihood that people will increasingly work from home in the coming years.
cambridge_speaking_strategies.translation: Hay una gran probabilidad de que [sujeto] cada vez [verbo] más en los próximos años.

cambridge_speaking_strategies.structure: If we choose this option, we are bound to face [problem/situation].
cambridge_speaking_strategies.example: If we choose this option, we are bound to face financial difficulties.
cambridge_speaking_strategies.translation: Si elegimos esta opción, es casi seguro que nos enfrentemos a [problema/situación].

cambridge_speaking_strategies.part: Part 2 (Speculating about what will happen next in the picture)
cambridge_speaking_strategies.structure: Judging by [evidence], it seems highly likely to me that [subject] is going to [verb].
cambridge_speaking_strategies.example: Judging by his expression, it seems highly likely to me that he is going to complain to the manager.
cambridge_speaking_strategies.translation: A juzgar por [evidencia], me parece muy probable que [sujeto] vaya a [verbo].

cambridge_speaking_strategies.structure: I'm going to have to say that [opinion], mainly because...
cambridge_speaking_strategies.example: I'm going to have to say that the first picture is more relevant, mainly because...
cambridge_speaking_strategies.translation: Voy a tener que decir que [opinión], principalmente porque...
